page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor running at 3.1 GHz, providing 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. Local storage is provided via a 600 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance supports a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is consistently weak, placing in the bottom 25% for stress-ng single-core, geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-core and memory-bound operations perform at an average level, placing in the middle 50% for stress-ng multi-core, geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks also align with average tier performance.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and the inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage, this instance is designed for memory-intensive workloads that require fast local scratch space. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving all register average performance tiers. The qualitative cost profile reflects a memory-optimized hardware class with bundled local storage, making it suitable for memory-bound databases, caching layers, and medium-scale data processing workloads where single-thread execution speed is not the primary bottleneck.
